verdict.summary: Discovering has a substantial Symfony application/discovery surface with explicit product identity, versioned and compatibility API contracts, security controls, observability, PHPUnit taxonomy, Playwright UI coverage, Composer quality gates, and documented RC evidence. Current read-only reconnaissance confirmed strict Composer validity, no known Composer security advisories, synchronized master at 0ff66ca86d6383f285ef11d2e73ecd6b602ae74d, and a previously passing Playwright result. The principal current concern is verification/tooling drift: repository code still uses src/EventSubscriber while the large canonicalization audit expects src/Subscriber/Discovery, so some historical canon/security evidence cannot be treated as freshly authoritative without reconciliation.
strengths: Clear resource-discovery product identity with public UI, management UI, JSON API, ranking, feedback, diagnostics, and operational discovery capabilities.
Explicit OpenAPI 3.1 contract covers versioned /api/v1/discovery operations plus deprecated compatibility endpoints.
Concrete endpoint protection includes management/write tokens, payload/content-type checks, rate limiting, correlation IDs, security headers, and request-surface policy.
Repository exposes Unit, Functional, Contract, Behavioral, and Playwright verification surfaces together with PHPStan and PHP-CS-Fixer quality gates.
Strict composer validation passed in this assessment and composer audit reported no known vulnerability advisories.
Local master is synchronized with origin/master at the assessed HEAD.
risks: Working tree was already dirty before assessment: .gating/README.md is deleted and AGENTS.md is modified; neither was changed during this READ_ONLY run.

Canonicalization audit expectations have drifted from the implemented namespace/topology: it expects src/Subscriber/Discovery and other older App-root paths while current classes remain under App\Discovering and src/EventSubscriber.
Because repository mutation is forbidden, test/runtime scripts that can create caches, databases, coverage, or result artifacts were not freshly executed.
Historical runtime and browser evidence is strong but does not substitute for a fresh current-HEAD behavioral/runtime pass.
No exact Git tag exists for the assessed HEAD.
next_actions: Reconcile tools/discovering_canon_audit.php and tools/security_preflight.php with the actual current canonical Symfony topology before treating those gates as authoritative.
After write/execution authority permits generated artifacts, run the declared ci:local, ci:runtime, ci:quality, schema, PHPUnit, behavioral coverage, and Playwright gates on the same HEAD.
Resolve or explicitly preserve the pre-existing AGENTS.md and .gating/README.md working-tree changes before release integration.

product.summary: Discovering has a well-defined resource-discovery product surface spanning human search, management workflows, APIs, relevance controls, feedback, and diagnostics.
risks: Product breadth is evidenced primarily by repository implementation/documentation rather than fresh end-user behavioral verification in this read-only run.
improvements: Refresh end-to-end evidence for the principal public and management workflows on the current HEAD.

architecture.summary: The repository has substantial Symfony-oriented separation across controllers, DTOs, entities, policies, factories, services, interfaces, repositories, resolvers, and value objects, but canonical audit rules and implemented topology are currently inconsistent.
risks: tools/discovering_canon_audit.php expects several paths/namespaces that no longer match the actual App\Discovering topology, weakening deterministic architecture-gate confidence.
improvements: Make the canonical audit describe the actual intended current architecture, then rerun it against the same revision.

runtime.summary: Runtime maturity is materially above the seeded baseline through explicit PHP 8.4/Symfony requirements, runtime preflight modes, console and HTTP entrypoints, Doctrine schema tooling, and historically recorded successful runtime acceptance.
risks: No fresh runtime execution was performed because the assessment is READ_ONLY and declared runtime/test scripts can create repository-local cache, database, or evidence artifacts.
improvements: On an execution-authorized pass, reuse the existing managed runtime and rerun runtime, console, schema, and behavioral checks without unnecessary restart.

qa.summary: QA posture is strong for a pre-RC component: four PHPUnit suites, Playwright browser tests, PHPStan, PHP-CS-Fixer, behavioral/UI coverage tooling, and prior recorded green acceptance materially exceed the previous seeded assessment.
risks: Current test-results only establishes a prior passing Playwright run; fresh same-HEAD PHPUnit and Playwright execution was intentionally not claimed.
improvements: Freshly execute Unit, Contract, Behavioral, Functional, static analysis, CS, behavioral coverage, and Playwright gates once artifact-producing verification is allowed.

ops.summary: Operational and security posture is materially implemented through request correlation, operation logging, token guards, mutation hardening, rate limiting, response security headers, OpenAPI documentation, and Composer security auditing.
risks: security_preflight.php validates legacy EventSubscriber paths and therefore requires reconciliation with the repository's intended canon before it can serve as a trustworthy canonical security gate.
improvements: Align security/canon preflight expectations, then rerun security, observability, OpenAPI, and runtime evidence gates.

market.summary: The component has coherent portfolio-facing positioning as a Symfony resource-discovery layer with explainable ranking, hybrid retrieval, management tooling, feedback learning, API exposure, and a deliberately bounded mission rather than generic search-engine scope.
risks: Repository evidence supports product positioning but does not provide external adoption, usage, or comparative market validation metrics.
improvements: Add measurable consumer/adoption evidence when available instead of inferring market strength solely from implementation breadth.

overall.summary: Discovering is materially closer to RC maturity than the seeded 7.7 snapshot suggests, with broad implementation and verification infrastructure, but a tooling/canon drift and absence of fresh artifact-producing runtime tests in this read-only window prevent a stronger current-HEAD verdict.
risks: Deterministic architecture/security gate drift can create false confidence until expected topology and actual implementation are reconciled.
Pre-existing dirty working-tree changes must remain isolated from release integration.
improvements: Reconcile deterministic gate definitions first, then perform one fresh same-HEAD full acceptance pass and visual verification before raising the RC score further.
